comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Experimentally determined the cropped limits of the vertical dash. Tested various layouts and positioning with Alex. Collected font assets for Alex.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Tried idea to build modulus function from pure arithmetic. Idea seems correct but the dash software for some reason just spits out the default value above 9. Reverted back to image selector idea. Used paint to concatenate two images, could probably pump out the full image set in one to two hours but sounds prone to error. Looked up Python libraries to make images. Used OpenCV and a for loop to build all images 0-99 needed. Loaded first 25 and test drove on live hardware. Adjusted speed variable to use GPS instead of AEM speed. Concept works. Extended idea to 200+ images to check memory constraints. Downloads take a little time but everything fits and the dash boots.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Built static proof image of dash to show team. Organized development directory and purged messy / no working code bits. Re-visited python script to combine images. Ran script again for both big and little numbers. Loaded all 400+ image assets into the dash program. Tested downloads working correct with increased memory demands.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Analyzed script that ChatGPT gave me to understand how it was working. Modified script for loops to have 00-99 and 000-999 for the little numbers. Created new image assets and organized into working directory to load into AEMDash. Sat and clicked ~2000 times to load all image selectors.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Finished uploading all 500 images to the dash program. Replaced static screen images with dynamic image selectors. Manually typed in all scenarios to round 0-254 for range. Tested background colors and removed pink border from testing. Re-loaded all images assets provided by Alex to verify I was using the correct ones. Met with Alex to discuss charge screen.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued adding in numbers to the rounding function for range. Downloaded new image set from Alex. Replaced on screen objects. Used alignment template to position things properly.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Picked up where I left off loading in new image assets. Verified I as using the latest for everything. Finished typing in channel to round estimated range from float to integer. Loaded all the charge bar images & discovered program too large to download. Deleted images until the exact max file size was found, ~8kB. Discussion with Alex about getting smaller images. Tried various methods to reduce memory.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Loaded new charge bar images and calculated memory difference. ~850kB less which should give enough room to add back in some of the other features. Test downloaded. Everything fits now.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Reviewed all onscreen objects and verified each and everyone functional and matches expected value. Test drove to verify additional calibration points. Reduced Warning and Fault screens by 35% and moved into display area. Added in condensed diag screen with core items, checked everything transferred correctly. Validated charge screen pulling up reasonable estimates.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Loaded correct temperature bar and splash images. Adjusted width for power bar. Tested new idea to reduce clicks necessary to make an image selector. Started on image selector for pack voltage.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Finished uploading images for Pack Voltage on the charge screen. Ran into the memory limit again. Started stripping out non-essential images and re-trying loading until the dash boots.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Loaded correct RND images and tested in vehicle. Corrected dash version numbers. Removed background box used for alignment.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Located Dash program and reduced memory until it would load. Moved Pack Volts back on to the charge screen. That display channel now only shows odd numbers between 330V and 370V. Charged for a bit. Added gauges to the new gauge sheet.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Opened the portrait dash design file and got back up to speed on remaining items. Looked into how I was able to make the temperature slider work, it has 17 possible values going from 0 to 80 by 5. Closest I can get to 20 to 80 is 22 to 78 by 3.5. Inputing this is very tedious so I'm saving it for the start of a day.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Adjusted the temperature scale on the digital dash to better suit the type W motor. Added new channels and a lookup table for a 16 to 80 scaling. Added in all the new number ranges for the channel doing the rounding then went to update the image selector which turns out can't handle floating point. Went back to the tedious brute force input method. Battled program memory useage getting too high and the dash no longer booting. Removed some charge bar photos to resolve that. Tested the temperature slider on the bench with the gauges program, mostly working now. Worked to get the no data message to turn on and timeout correctly. Added in a change log and verified verion numbers correct on the boot and diag screens.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued digital dash work. Checked PRD was in the right order. Added Pack_Current to the charge screen by filling out another image selector with all the associated variables and logic to round and filter that signal. Tested charging to verify functionality. Ivanhoe showing 13% SOC now. Checked the total energy accum on the pack and multiplied that by the current SOC based on cell voltage alone. Added this new number to the energy counter and set that as the new PackMaxCapacity. Results show a change from 32,000 kWh to 38,000 kWh in comparison to the 36,000 kWh we ended up with in Berke.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Started on a more automated dash / gauges checkout program but couldn't really figure out a format that would work and be done today. Used Claude to organize all the signals that are used on the dash into a single DBC as a happy medium. Now I don't have to dig through a list with hundreds and hundreds of signals 41 times to fully validate a set of gauges or dash. Used new DBC with old gauges test program to verify the latest dash program. Fixed a few minor things and removed the temporary development widgets. Added in a PackVoltage image selector to the charge screen using a new MUCH easier dash technique I found. Still need to strip out any addition un-used pictures and load into the vehicle.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued loading the numbers from 300 to 405 one by one for the pack volts image selector. Stripped all un-used images from the file saving some memory which puts the dash further away from where it instantly doesn't boot. Loaded the program into the vehicle and verified the basics working as expected.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Methodically walked through all the widgets for the main screen and charge screen substituting values and watching how they worked on screen. Corrected various issues along the way. Completed 11/13 of the complicated widgets.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Finished checking the various widgets while taking thorough status notes. Loaded the screen to the vehicle and gave a basic look over. Posted notes to Slack.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Ivanhoe Alfa Dash: Finished checking widgets and making any improvements along the way. Thoroughly documented all the backend work and posted to Slack. Developed new logic for PND which still need to be better tested on a dry day. Fed a bunch of screen shots of DashDesign to Claude and developed a list of everything that makes the Warning and Fault lamps trigger. Collected other resources and built a prompt that resulted in a test tool that send CAN messages like the VCU would but without having to sit down and reason what each value should be and then go find it somewhere in a giant list. Used the tool to check warning and fault lamps. Wrote up summary of the day.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Troubleshooting for BMS fault now showing on the dash and gauges. Disabled fault reporting for thermistor channels BMSM1_G03_Therm3 & BMSM1_G06_Therm3 since they seemed way out of range (disconnected) and were causing a BMS fault. Fault still shows up in VCU but apparently doesn't do anything. Checked dash and narrowed down a second fault to upgraded BMS firmware. Corrected the false flag in the dash logic.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Loaded the Berke calibration into the vehicle. Started charging the vehicle up to the top but not getting current for some reason. Found many checkout items haven't been looked at. Ran through the entire checkout sheet from top to bottom and added items to the formatted punch list. Posted for team.

comments.author: Devin DuMont

Flashed the latest Berke firmware burn and updated gear ratio and pedal calibration, and pack capacity. Added all these changes into the tracking sheet. Reviewed completeness in the rest of the sheet. Need to at a minimul check the inverter settings.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Verified energy counters messed up due to incorrect current direction. Inverted the IVT direction and left on charge.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text:
Reviewed compare reports again between Berke and Ivanhoe. Produced a list of required differences and what those configuration options should be for Ivanhoe. Checked energy counters, still massively off after one charge cycle. Reflashed Berke Rev5 firmware burn to get the "reset" option. Transfered the compare report settings in. Verified everything set correctly, backed up this calibrations and sent off to AEM for a firmware burn. Charged to the top alongside watching energy counters, pack resistance, etc. making sure everything looked within reason. Couldn't average the CellR values like I usually do since the pack was too high but the initial calculation was within spec. Clicked through the digital dash making note problems due to the VCU200_15 build with an Elcon charger and DCDC, as well as portrait layout oddities. Test drove verifying top end limiters. The digital dash doesn't have a logger but I manually pulled the logs and used my existing scripts to convert to CSV. Imported the logs for plotting and verified the limiters plot looked consistent with the cell specs. Made final backups of the inverter and PMU. Flashed the firmware burn and left on charge.

For review, here's the Berke To Ivanhoe Delta
        APP1_Min        1.110        1.130
        APP2_Min        0.560        0.570
        DriveGearRatio        4.10        4.56
        DriveTireDiameter        23.44        24.80
        PackCurrentPolarity        Invert        ---
        PackMaxCapacity        36000        32000

Ivanhoe ToDo's Before Shipping
        Get wifi credentials, upload, verify configuration sync'd.
        Finish Digital Dash (Remove EGT/CCU readings, Add charge confirmation, Correct portrait visual problems)
        Test drive, verify lower limiters, make plots for pack consumption, temps, & low limiters.
        Verify running temps and InvTempRefOption.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued Dash work. Removed more image assets to give a little more memory headroom. Used Claude to make an additional image asset to properly label the pack current channel. Loaded this and tested for boot stability. Added in missing message for low SOC warning. Tested gauges to make sure warning light came on in various scenarios. Verified PackMaxCapacity was set up higher, test drove and checked limiters. Sent firmware off to AEM for a second burn.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Flashed the firmware burn, checked various options looked correct, left on the charger overnight.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Organized and reduced the ten or so partial efforts to convert and decode logs. Ended up with single well organized directory with tools compatible with our logger that AI could use to properly digest data. Organized DBC files specific to AEM and copied them over to the Conversion Tools directory changing their format as required. Manually downloaded logs from the CANcloud for the charge the evening of July 7th and manually ran them through the conversion process. This conversion process is now setup correctly to have AI repeat without ever getting the "Oh you're right, good for you to push back" instead of garbage presented as fact. Fed all the previous into an open conversation and had Claude build a report of the failure. Reviewed analysis and posted for the team.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Re-downloaded the logs from yesterday and added in some additional logs to make sure that the recharge was captured, Converted these and gave them to Claude along with AEM manuals, an exported calibration, and additional context about how this charger works. Went back and forth evaluating and dismissing various theories proposed based off of actual experience with what option does what and what parts of logic in the VCU don't work and are bypassed on purpose. Built a CSV plotter with the log data, clicked around a little bit and ultimately became very concerned about how basic plots don't look as expected. Told this to Claude & continued discussing with the team. Ultimately decided the charge not starting is not a problem.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued back and forth with Claude and various Slack correspondence with Marc.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: (Last night) Built a log replay script with Claude to get the CSS logs into the AEM format for analysis. (Today) Tested the log replay script which crashed immediatly. Let Claude debug everything with actual hardware in auto mode. Got everything working and tested the process to get a CSS log into AEMData. All looked good so I set the whole charge failure to play back at 10x speed while logging, overloaded the bus. Will setup to run over night and check back in tomorrow.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued work on the log replay tool. Added a way to change the playback speed and worked on the display setup to be logging all the critical channels. Tried logging but started getting bus overload errors with CAN2 and CAN3 merged.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Setup the log playback tool with 1M baud to hopefully eliminate bus overload issues. Played back the very start of the log and got useable results. Let run for a while to get a fuller log to test. Removed not applicable items from the diag screen and verified logic and CAN messages associated with the gauges, couldn't get the VCU turned off with the digital dash still turned on to test the signal chain. Trying alternative methods tomorrow.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued diag and correspondence with AEM. Used Claude to better understand the problem & analyzed plots on my own. Decided there's nothing more we can do about the issue.

During testing found a reliable way to force a weak charge. Repeated this procedure until I caught it on a log. Analyzed and posted to Slack.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Ran various ISO-SPI tests with Justin changing the number of groups on the BMS chain and observinng the results. Couldn't narrow down an exact hardware failure but did eliminate a number of theories. Called AEM and bounced ideas back and forth.

comments.text: Used AEMCal to verify BMS now reportinng all satellites correctly.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Met with the team and reviewed status. Pulled logs, corrupted as expected. Cleared logs and did a quick test drive to verify working. Tracked down software versions for the DashBox and the digital dash to determine which BRAKE warning lamp logic was in use.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: The two lights in Avalos are TEMP (Amber) and BRAKE (Red). The BRAKE lamp is the Fault Summary which has a significant number of things it's looking at, a lot of them are pretty important which merits looking into making this. Most the individual signals are logged but the summary is not logged due to technical difficulties. This means there's no marker in the log to find when the problem was. Tried a number of ways to get the fault logs useable, none worked. Trying Claude next.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Determining current checkout status. Added Billy's Wi Fi to the logger and verified connectivity. Compared the VCU calibration to the latest GMC calibration. Determined a fuller upgrade process is needed.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Flashed the vehicle with the Hastert firmware burn. Reset options and reviewed compare report. Started going through options one by one.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Reviewed precharge settings and transfered over some required for the LDU vs a Cascadia motor. Hooked up the MSD and tested precharge, had to adjust some more seemingly unrelated settings to get a success. Tested putting the inverter in PWM mode and driving forward / backwards several inches.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Went over precharge settings and adjusted slightly to get a faster precharge with less pack voltage delta when the positive contactor pulls in. Reviewed charge related settings and charged up to ~370 Volts. Forced in a CellR during this charge but kept running into cells jumping between 0.005 mOhms and ~70 mOhms between trials. Having these correct impacts torque limiting. Upgraded the digital dash to the latest version 2.31 and branched that to a LDU specific one, adjusted the temperature channel to RTD1. Still need to do more digital dash and gauges validation.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued forcing Cell R and got it to settle down at 0.55 mOhms per cell. Set this as the default and continued charging. Monitored till the top and checked that the energy counters reset and the vehicle shut off properly. Copied over SOC and range tables and verified they were for Tesla modules in a SUV. Checked on the CAN bus that two thermistors in group 6 were causing a fault to show up. Disabled faults for these two thermistors. Reviewed the limiters for cell voltage, pack SOC, and temperature. Still need to test drive and verify the limiters, then get a firmware burn.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Verified charge ended correctly. Pack voltage was 396V which seemed a little bit low, looked for reasoning in the log and the charge did finish at 399 V but must have been warm and just settled out over the weekend. Adjusted the charge to voltage to 400 V and topped off the charge. Drove to test the limiters initially getting heavy cutting in and out between SOC and Cell Max. Compared torque map between the GMC and the previous Avalos calibration, repeated for the limiter set. Everything looks okay must be due to the different gear ratio. Increased the SOC blanket limiter down to 80% and re-tested with Billy as the driver so I could monitor. Still getting a limiter cut-out and need to re-adjust some more. Left on charge for the evening.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Went online with the VCU to continue fine tuning the limiters and noticed pack voltage at 229 Volts with 3 BMS groups missing. Verified reading on the CAN bus and checked actual pack voltage from the IVT at 396 Volts. Continued troubleshooting from the VCU and then tried a few key cycles and pulling 12V at the battery. No luck.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Reviewed the limiters against several previous Avalos calibrations and the current Hastert calibration. Most were the same with Hastert being more protective, made some slight modifications to increase this. Turned on creep and copied over the related settings from Berke. Test drove to collect logs and evaluate creep smoothness. Charged to the top again and test drove with additional channels in the log to tell me which limiter is on when. Analyzed data, need one more round to get to acceptable.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Looked around in the VCU for a rate limiter that applys to the transition between SOC and Cell_Max limiters, couldn't find anything and it probably doesn't exist. Asked Scott just incase. Used the logs collected yesterday to determine the exact SOC and Cell_Max that the limiter are flopping between, adjusted their ranges to have a similar derating when they transition then shifted the SOC limiter slightly heavier so it would be favored. Charged back up to the very top and test drove. Also reviewed plots from yesterday and noticed increasing the OCV first order filter TC from 2s to 10s didn't show up in the OCV variable getting used for SOC and then eventually wasn't impacting the torque limiters. Continued log analysis & trials before landing on a fully fuctional calibration that Billy thinks drives well. Had Marc test drive also.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Reviewed yesterdays work and compared calibration against other vehicles in the fleet looking for any gotchas. Updated checkout sheet to fully reflect vehicle progress.  Wrote up email about OCV dipping issue and sent firmware off to AEM for a burn. Verified and fixed various notes found in the checkout sheet. Talked to AEM on the phone for a while about the OCV dip problem, looked at the raptor logic with Scott. Determined several tests to run to understand the filter TC's and ran them, analyzed results and determined whole new VCU200 build would be required to get the current configuration any better. Discussion with Marc and held off on the firmware burn for more testing.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Troubleshot SOC dip by experimentally changing values in the SOC K Factor table and watching the results. Determined the SOC not using Coloumb counting at all because too few charge cycles have been completed, could not find a channel with the current count of charge cycles. Wrote email to AEM to verify all this.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: When through any and all notes for the truck looking for remaining items to tend to. Charged up to the top and modified SOC_EstimateBeforeChargeCycles to various numbers while watching SOC to determine how many "valid" charges there were. Looks like that critera is only met 2/3 so far which means it needs one more charge. Pulled current inverter settings and reviewed LDU EEPROM against latest profiles. Organized the LDU / SDU directories a little better.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Shuffled around cars and chargers till I could get both Ivanhoe and Avalos charging. Plugged in Avalos and monitored charge near the top. Saw PackFullyCharged_Count drop from 2 to 1 and then count back up to 3. Seems like a bug of some sort but with lowering SOC_EstimateBeforeChargeCycles to 1 it might not matter. Asked AEM about that and put in a request for another firmware burn. Test drove with SOC now on Coloumb counting and monitored CellMax, SOC dip, regen smoothness, etc. verified in logs. Wrote up the results and posted to Slack.

comments.author: Justin Landry
comments.text:
@Alex Noonan @Marc Davis  PDI Findings.

Overall wirings and hoses could use more zip ties and securing and existing ones need tails cut.
LDU forward Motor mount contacts the bolt head thats holding the bracket on.
AC Charger wiring dangling down near rear shock.
Front fender liners are loose and or missing fasteners on both sides.
Rear battery hardlines rattling around and not secured.
Ebrake adjustment lock nuts all loose where it turns from one cable into 2.
!!!Both inner drive shaft CVs at the LDU seem to be slinging grease.
Lets check front and rear axle Ubolt nuts and mark them tight.
Front and rear diff vent hosed damaged or not secured. (front is just jammed up between brake lines)
Check all body mounts, 2 on the drivers side completely loose.
Top/hardshell creaks/squeaks a bit. (prob not much to do about it)
!!!vehicle drives ok but i felt like i was struggling to keep it in a straight line. it feels like it sticks in positions. maybe too much drag from the double dampers but it felt not great to me.
Right defrost vent popping out of dash.
A red backlight dot appears in the speedo gauge when the headlights are turned on. is this by design or some funky backlighting?
Reverse lights were INOP
Rear view mirror floppy.
Slight looseness in the steering but it seems like its in the steering box and its a big ole truck. might be totally normal.
Magnetic MSD cover missing.
Radiator core support missing hardware
Brake fluid a little low
Power steering fluid very low
12V battery mount very floppy
A/C compressor mount missing hardware and flopping around
Power steering pump flopping around. mount looks too light duty for it.
A/C lines from compressor are not secured and cable clamp is falling off.
Power steering return line quite cracked at both ends with no hose clamps.( might be wrong type of hose and fluid is degrading it.
No marking compound on any steering, suspension or brake components. would be nice to have everything double checked and marked as tight.
Overall wiring in this vehicle is quite messy, most likely due to all the various repairs and revisions to the car over the years.
HV going into LDU has a very tight bend and no support on it. is also rubbing on the frame.
!!! AC charger input to the OBC connector looks blackened/burned!!!!
No license plate.
Charge test passes ish. wakes up, starts charging but relays odd numbers. Known issue by marc and Devin.

Still need to check tire pressures and lug torque when we dive into these things.

comments.text:
This morning i was back on the blazer. took a look at the brakes, the booster had got out of sync. reset the adjustment at the pedal an the brakes came back. tested function with a few more key cycles and they were working.
Moved onto the rear vehicle lighting. after yesterdays advice that the reverse lights were always on i started by confirming this. we found that it had changed and that no turn signals were working now but the brakes and reverse were. started some diag and checking fuses, then found that someone had inspected the steering column and then found that the wiring had been pulled down, pulled apart and not installed correctly. 2 pins were pushed back and the connector was only half connected. re secured the connector and all lighting came back.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Diag for clicking contactor during charge. Started charge and over rode contactors to narrow down which one was clicking. Ended up being a channel marked spare that actually had heater bricks on it. Changed this channel from Wake to Battery Pump which should stay always on during charging and driving. Should review logs to verify this behavior.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Re-organized and moved gauge checkout information to the vehicles sheet. Marked done. Disabled the LEM sensor. Don't see any faults in the VCU but should also check the CAN bus. Ran through the checkout sheet updating items. Posted for the team with additional status details.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Charged the vehicle up till 402.3 but charge doesn't seem to shutdown. Troubleshot a bit and ended up sending logs to AEM.  Verified correct SOC profile for the pack was being used. Marked off a few extra miscellaneous items in the checkout sheet and updated the punch card.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Reviewed various charge for related settings to verify they matched as expected. Monitored the CAN bus for the VCU request for voltage and current and noticed that current was set at zero even with the correct voltage. Moved back to the VCU and reviewed various current limits and found CCL was set to zero. Looked into the configuration for that and changed it from CellR based back to temperature based and reviewed the temperature tables. Monitored charge for another couple of minutes and it shut down correctly. Fed Claude exported AEM calibration files and several manuals for AEM then asked for a summary with default settings with a startup guide. Unfortunately Claude turned two ~40 page manuals into one 259 page guide with way more content to validate and review making the strategy not worthful on the first attempt. Reviewed the high level limiters and took the vehicle for a test drive to verify cell max under regen and adjusted the torque table with Marc.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Updated the pedal calibration. Ran various stomp cycles slow and fast to ensure the cable wasn't sticking and that the cross check between channels was 1 percent or so. Exported the torque tables for Hopkins and Miner. Wrote a Python script to interpolate the 10x10 dimensional torque table to a 19x19 dimension torque table that the VCU300 requires. Provided information and an explanation to Marc as a starting point for his tuning. Pulled AEMDash logs and troubleshot coolant temp warning showing up. Temperature did indeed spike when the pump was not running, The VCU was requesting the pump to run the entire time, and the log shows pump failing the previous key cycle, suspected air bubbles that causes that specific pump to shut down internally. Raised the regen limit from -50 to -100 Nm.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Test drove with Marc and adjusted limiters and pack capacity. Also enabled creep and tuned.
